method: Read630 additional lifecycle/conversation/memory-helper lines. Compiled unchanged extract_agent_memory_items with owned synthetic ASCII and Unicode inputs.
findings: Confirmed Unicode panic in unchanged extract_agent_memory_items: it finds marker byte offset in lowercased copy then slices original string. Input İremember я causes non-char-boundary slicing, caught in isolated harness; remember tea control returns tea. No original application process launched.

This is the same general lowercase-offset hazard already noted in other preview helpers, but independently reproduced in this function. Local rrrah implementation not changed or declared defective from upstream result.

Remember Last Position persists monitor center rather than exact launcher pixel position; Custom Monitor chooses second enumeration entry. These source behaviors narrow feature wording; no multimonitor runtime test.

animate_window and do_show both trigger_search on common non-AI show path, incrementing generation and enqueueing twice. Workers coalesce queued requests, but duplicate work before second enqueue remains possible; no timing/performance measurement.

do_hide resets query/homepage and hides window but does not cancel AI workers. reset_visible_chat_view explicitly resets visible state while background DB updates continue; this is documented intended behavior, not proof of cancelled computation.

format_conversation splits prompt and response using unescaped text separator lines. Literal user/assistant content containing separators can be interpreted as additional turns. No conversation roundtrip fixture in this batch.

Local command runner uses output capture with no timeout/cancellation/output-size cap in read function. All command strings are reviewed source data; no command runner or source-provided action executed.
limits: No production changes; no Windows integration or actual agent/clipboard/network actions.

executed_controls.output: ASCII control passed; Unicode lowercase-offset panic reproduced
executed_controls.scope: Synthetic inputs against exact extracted original function, not upstream UI or full tests.
